title: What Is STOTT Pilates? Mat vs Reformer and Getting Started
seoTitle: What Is STOTT Pilates? Mat vs Reformer
description: STOTT Pilates is a contemporary teaching method with five stated principles. How Mat and Reformer differ, and what a first session usually involves.
primaryQuestion: What is STOTT Pilates, and how do Mat and Reformer sessions differ?
directAnswer: STOTT Pilates is a contemporary, anatomically based approach to the Pilates method taught through Merrithew’s training programmes. Merrithew lists five basic principles that organise how you breathe and place the body: breathing, pelvic placement, rib cage placement, scapular movement and stabilisation, and head and neck placement. Mat and Reformer are delivery formats (floor work versus spring-resisted equipment), not rival brands. The method name describes how a session is taught; it does not prove better outcomes than every other Pilates style.

sections.heading: What the STOTT method refers to
paragraphs: Pilates as a whole is a system of controlled exercises emphasising breath, alignment and organised strength. According to Merrithew’s own FAQs, STOTT Pilates is a contemporary approach to Joseph Pilates’ original method, refined with modern exercise-science ideas. Saying “STOTT” points to that teaching framework and certification pathway; it does not, by itself, tell you whether you will work on a mat or on a machine.

Merrithew’s five basic principles page names: breathing; pelvic placement; rib cage placement; scapular movement and stabilisation; and head and neck placement. Those cues help organise effort so the neck and lower back are not doing work meant for elsewhere. They are teaching tools, not a medical diagnosis of your posture and not independent proof that pain will resolve after a few classes.
Merrithew marketing language about being among the safest or most effective methods is branding. This site does not treat those claims as comparative clinical evidence.

sections.heading: How Mat sessions differ from Reformer sessions
paragraphs: Mat sessions use the floor, with body weight and gravity providing most of the challenge. Small props may appear. Mat work can travel into home practice of patterns you have already learned in a coached session, though a class is still supervised movement, not a random downloaded circuit. Advanced Mat sequences can be demanding on control.

A Reformer is a sliding carriage with springs, straps and a footbar. Springs can assist or resist, which allows finely graded loading when an instructor sets them thoughtfully. Reformer sessions need the equipment; you cannot recreate the exact feel with a yoga mat alone. Cost, studio access and class size shape the choice as much as preference.

Neither format automatically rehabilitates diastasis, pelvic pain or incontinence. Both can be adapted when the instructor understands your limits. Tell the instructor about pregnancy, recent birth, surgery or pain, and stop if pain or dizziness occurs.

sections.heading: What a first session typically involves
paragraphs: Expect an introduction to the principles, a warm-up that may include breathing and placement drills, then a sequence matched to your level. Ask whether the class is Mat or Reformer, how many people share the instructor, and how modifications work mid-session. Wear comfortable clothes; grip socks are often useful on Reformer.

Dr. Zalak Shah (PT) is a STOTT Pilates Instructor (Mat & Reformer). At Women’s Health Duo, Mat Pilates is offered online; in-person sessions are in Bangalore and Ahmedabad. A Pilates hour is movement coaching. It is not the same product as a physiotherapy assessment for leakage, pelvic pain or abdominal-wall rehab. See women’s health physiotherapy when symptoms lead.

sections.heading: How a class differs from physiotherapy
paragraphs: A physiotherapy visit is a clinical service: history, examination and a plan tied to your goals. A Pilates class is skilled group or private coaching within a fitness frame. Even when the instructor is also a physiotherapist, a mixed-level class is usually not a full medical assessment of every participant.

If your goal is symptom care, ask whether assessment should come before a busy fitness class. What Pilates is, including mat and equipment formats, is a separate page. This page stays with the STOTT method.

faqs.question: Is STOTT Pilates the same as a Reformer machine?
faqs.answer: No. STOTT names a teaching method. Reformer names a piece of equipment. You can have STOTT-based Mat classes or STOTT-based Reformer classes; the timetable abbreviation should say which format you are booking.

faqs.question: Do I need Reformer to benefit from STOTT principles?
faqs.answer: No. Merrithew applies the same five basic principles to Mat and equipment work. Reformer offers spring resistance; Mat uses body weight. Suitability depends on goals, access and how well the session is coached for your body.
